chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Isḥāq al-Madāʾinī, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive in the land spreading corruption..."

About the verse—what is that action which, when he does it, makes one of these four penalties binding? He عليه السلام said: “If he wages war against Allah and His Messenger and strives in the land spreading corruption, then if he kills, he is killed for it; if he kills and takes wealth, he is killed and crucified; if he takes wealth and does not kill, his hand and foot are cut off on opposite sides; and if he unsheathes the sword, thus waging war against Allah and His Messenger and striving in the land spreading corruption, but does not kill and does not take wealth, he is banished from the land.” I said: How is he banished, and what is the limit of his banishment? He said: “He is banished from the town in which he did what he did to another town, and the people of that town are written to that he is an exile, so they are not to sit with him, nor trade with him, nor marry him, nor eat with him, nor drink with him. That is done to him for one year. Then if he leaves that town for another, they are written to with the like of that until the year is completed.” I said: What if he heads to the land of shirk to enter it? He said: “If he heads to the land of shirk to enter it, its people are fought.”
(527) 144 - Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Isḥāq, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام:
The like of it, and he added in it: “That is done for one year, for he will repent before that while humbled.” He said: I said: If he heads for the land of shirk to enter it? He said: “He is killed.”

key_terms.أَرْضِ الشِّرْكِ: the land of shirk, meaning territory identified with unbelief outside the Muslim domain
key_terms.صُلِبَ: he is crucified, one of the punishments mentioned for the gravest form of the crime
key_terms.فَسَادًا: corruption, meaning unlawful disorder and harm spread in the land
key_terms.مَنْفِيٌّ: an exile, one formally declared banished to the people of another town
key_terms.مِنْ خِلَافٍ: on opposite sides, meaning the hand and foot are cut from opposite sides
key_terms.نُفِيَ: he is banished, meaning expelled from the land or locality with enforced social exclusion
key_terms.يُحَارِبُونَ: they wage war, meaning violent rebellion or armed hostility that brings public corruption

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the punishments mentioned in the verse about waging war against Allah and spreading corruption on earth?
ai.summary: This narration explains the legal application of the verse concerning those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and spread corruption in the land. It distinguishes the prescribed punishments according to whether the offender killed, took property, or merely brandished the sword, and it further explains the meaning of banishment and its social consequences.
